subject: AWS Marketplace: pricing/activation & usage routing
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Peters <emily.peters@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace: pricing/activation & usage routing

Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Wanted to summarize the practical next steps for getting Acme set up on AWS Marketplace (SaaS Metering + Fulfillment) so we can align procurement and engineering expectations. High level:

- Confirm usage dimension mapping (what counts as a billable unit)
- Agreement on entitlement activation flow (Marketplace entitlement -> Acme account provisioning)
- Billing reconciliation cadence & webhook payloads for usage reports
- Schedule a short tech call with CloudBroker to validate the entitlement ID exchange

Attached is a preliminary mapping we used with another retail customer — it'll save time. Can you confirm: (A) which SKU(s) you plan to expose on the Marketplace, and (B) whether your procurement requires monthly invoices or consolidated annual billing statements?

Proposed mini-MAP (mutual action plan):
1) Acme confirms SKUs + intended consumption metric (by Fri 14 May)
2) Redwood shares entitlement mapping file + webhook spec (Mon 17 May)
3) CloudBroker and Acme run entitlement activation smoke test (week of 24 May)

If that timeline looks tight, say so and we’ll stretch. CC'ing Rishi/Ben to flag any contract/pricing constraints on our side.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

[Attachment: SaaS_Entitlement_Map.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Emily Peters <emily.peters@acmeretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: pricing/activation & usage routing

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- SKUs: We'll initially expose two SKUs: "Acme Insights - Standard" and "Acme Insights - Enterprise".
- Usage metric: we want metering by "monthly active model invocations" (we track invocations server-side and can emit counts).
- Billing: Procurement prefers monthly invoices consolidated per AWS account. They will not accept per-invocation invoices to multiple payors — so marketplace should send usage to Acme's AWS account and AWS will bill us.

Questions:
1) On entitlement activation — once a customer purchases via the Marketplace, can we get an entitlement webhook that includes the buyer AWS account ID and the SKU?
2) Will Redwood provide a recommended mapping to translate "model invocation" counts into the marketplace usage dimension?

We'll review the attached mapping and respond with SKU IDs by EOD Friday. Also copying our procurement team for any legal/PO items.

Appreciate it,
Emily Peters
Director of Cloud Ops, Acme Retail
emily.peters@acmeretail.com

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Peters <emily.peters@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, CloudBroker Onboarding <marketplace-onboarding@cloudbroker.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: pricing/activation & usage routing

Emily —

Appreciate the quick clarification. Short answers to your questions:

1) Yes — AWS Marketplace can surface the buyer's AWS Account ID in the entitlement notification; we recommend using the marketplace entitlement ID combined with the buyer account ID to provision Acme access. CloudBroker will help validate the exact payload and timing.

2) We will take the raw "invocations" metric and propose a usage dimension that is compatible with AWS Marketplace (name: "acme.invocations.v1"). See the attached ENTITLEMENT map — it includes two mapping options: a 1:1 invocation-to-unit or a bucketed model (100 invocations = 1 billing unit). The bucketed model usually smooths spikes and is less noisy for retail workloads.

I've uploaded the current file to the shared drive and linked the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2027-0217.

Action items for clarity:
- Emily: confirm preferred mapping (1:1 or bucketed) and provide the SKU names you gave us in the Marketplace UI by EOD Fri 14 May.
- CloudBroker: please confirm webhook sample payload and whether you require a test buyer account for staging.
- Rishi/Ben: flag any billing or contract constraints (especially around minimum monthly commitments).

Attaching the entitlement mapping file and a draft SLA addendum that covers usage reporting latency expectations.

Jordan

[Attachment: SaaS_Entitlement_Map.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: Draft_SLA_Addendum.docx (docx)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: pricing/activation & usage routing

Looping in legal/contracting context — quick internal note:

- Procurement preference for monthly consolidated invoices is fine; AWS will bill Acme and we’ll receive downstream settlement as usual. We need to ensure our fulfillment contract supports the buyer-provided AWS Account ID as the single source of truth for entitlement.
- Two negotiation points to surface: (1) minimum monthly commitment vs pure usage; (2) SLA addendum language around usage-reporting window (we should cap reporting lag at 48 hours in the SLA).
- For pricing: if Acme is open to a small ramp (e.g., 20% discount for a 12-month commit for Enterprise SKU), that simplifies go-live and may help us avoid complex proration issues in Marketplace terms.

Jordan — please keep Acme's procurement looped; Marissa can lead the pricing approval on our side. Ben, can you schedule a 30-min slot with CloudBroker and Acme for the entitlement payload walkthrough?

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Peters <emily.peters@acmeretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, CloudBroker Onboarding <marketplace-onboarding@cloudbroker.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@acmeretail.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: pricing/activation & usage routing

Jordan/Rishi/CloudBroker —

This looks straightforward and aligns with our procurement expectations. Quick notes:

- We will start with the bucketed mapping (100 invocations = 1 billing unit) to reduce noise.
- SKUs confirmed: "Acme Insights - Standard" (SKU: ACME-STD-01) and "Acme Insights - Enterprise" (SKU: ACME-ENT-01).
- We agree to a 30-day reporting lag cap in the initial docs but are open to the 48-hour target if Redwood can include that in the SLA addendum.

Please schedule the entitlement payload call — Wed 19 May 10:00 AM PT works for our engineers. Ben, can you confirm? Once we have the webhook sample and a staging buyer account, we'll run the activation smoke test.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this live.

Emily Peters
Director of Cloud Ops, Acme Retail
